weight_scale.note: Weights are additive ranking points, not probabilities. Within one fault, rules that share a 'group' read the same underlying evidence, so only the strongest supporting and strongest contradicting rule in each group count.

rules.rationale: The battery fuel gauge reports a fault condition.
limitations: Reported by the battery management system; a technician should confirm with a load test.

rules.rationale: The battery management system reports an overheat condition.
limitations: Can also be caused by a hot environment or heavy use during the scan.

rules.rationale: Battery temperature at or above 45 C while connected to a computer is unusually high.
limitations: Single point-in-time reading; charging and heavy use raise temperature normally.

rules.rationale: The fuel gauge estimates the battery holds less than 80% of its design capacity, a common replacement threshold.
limitations: Fuel-gauge estimate, not a lab measurement.

rules.rationale: Estimated capacity is 80-87% of design: noticeable wear, but usually not yet the cause of severe problems.
limitations: Fuel-gauge estimate, not a lab measurement.

rules.rationale: Estimated capacity is at least 92% of design, which argues against a worn battery.
limitations: Does not rule out a battery that cannot deliver peak current.

rules.rationale: 800+ charge cycles is beyond the rated life of most phone batteries.
limitations: Cycle counting methods differ between manufacturers.

rules.rationale: 500-800 cycles: many batteries are approaching the end of rated life.
limitations: Cycle counting methods differ between manufacturers.

rules.rationale: Lithium-ion batteries in phones older than about 2.5 years have usually lost meaningful capacity.
limitations: Based on typical ageing, not on this battery.

rules.rationale: A battery replaced within the last year is less likely to be worn (unless it was a low-quality part).
limitations: Low-quality replacement batteries can fail early.

rules.rationale: Sudden percentage drops are a classic sign of a worn battery whose voltage sags under load.
limitations: Customer-reported.

rules.rationale: Fast drain even when idle points to either reduced capacity or a background process keeping the phone awake.
limitations: Customer-reported; Safe Mode helps separate the two causes.

rules.rationale: Fast drain only during heavy use is largely expected behaviour.
limitations: Customer-reported.

rules.rationale: Switching off with charge remaining usually means the battery cannot sustain voltage under load.
limitations: Customer-reported; a faulty power-management chip can cause the same symptom.

rules.rationale: Aged batteries lose much of their output in the cold.
limitations: Even healthy batteries can shut down in very cold conditions.

rules.rationale: Spontaneous reboots are most often caused by system crashes, sometimes by power delivery problems.
limitations: Customer-reported.

rules.rationale: A lifting screen or back cover is most commonly caused by a swelling battery.
limitations: Customer-reported; a technician must confirm.

notes.text: A swelling battery can catch fire. Stop charging the phone, do not press on it, and have it inspected as soon as possible.

rules.rationale: The OS recorded that the last restart was caused by a power fault (e.g. under-voltage).
limitations: Boot reasons are vendor-specific and occasionally mislabelled.

rules.rationale: The OS recorded that the last restart was caused by a kernel crash or watchdog reset.
limitations: Kernel crashes can also have hardware causes (e.g. memory or power faults).

rules.rationale: The OS recorded a thermal shutdown.
limitations: Heavy use in a hot environment can cause this on a healthy phone.

rules.rationale: Several abnormal restarts were recorded in the last 7 days.
limitations: Restart history is not recorded on many devices.

rules.rationale: The OS logged crashes of core system components in the last 7 days.
limitations: System crashes can occasionally be triggered by failing hardware.

rules.rationale: 15 or more app crashes/freezes were logged in the last 7 days.
limitations: One misbehaving app can produce many entries.

rules.rationale: Several app crashes/freezes were logged in the last 7 days.
limitations: Occasional crashes are normal on most phones.

rules.rationale: The customer reports crashes, but the OS logged none in the available history. This is conflicting evidence.
limitations: Some freezes are not logged as crashes; the history may have been cleared by a restart or reset.

rules.rationale: Whole-phone freezes and launcher restarts point to system-level instability.
limitations: Customer-reported.

rules.rationale: Many different apps crashing suggests a system-wide software or storage problem.
limitations: Customer-reported.

rules.rationale: Crashes limited to one or two apps are usually an app problem, fixable by updating or reinstalling it.
limitations: Customer-reported.

notes.text: Crashes limited to one or two apps are usually fixed by updating, clearing data for, or reinstalling those apps.

rules.rationale: Problems that start right after an update are frequently software-related.
limitations: Timing can be coincidental.

rules.rationale: If the problem disappears in Safe Mode, a third-party app is the likely cause.
limitations: Customer-reported; intermittent problems can disappear by chance.

rules.rationale: A problem that persists in Safe Mode is less likely to be caused by a third-party app.
limitations: System software can still be at fault.

rules.rationale: The customer reports crashes or slowness.
limitations: Customer-reported symptom area only.

rules.rationale: Heat while idle usually means a runaway background process, or less often a battery fault.
limitations: Customer-reported.

rules.rationale: Excess heat while charging can come from a worn battery or a poor connection in the charging path.
limitations: Fast charging makes phones noticeably warm by design.

rules.rationale: The OS reported severe thermal throttling during the scan, while the phone should be nearly idle.
limitations: Point-in-time reading; charging from the computer adds heat.

rules.rationale: Less than 5% free storage severely degrades Android performance and prevents updates.
Less than 10% free storage can slow the phone and cause app failures.
At least 20% of storage is free, so storage pressure is unlikely.
The customer regularly sees the phone's own 'storage full' warnings or update failures, which the OS shows only when free space is critically low.
limitations: Customer-reported; confirm free space in Settings > Storage.

rules.rationale: The customer reports storage warnings as a main problem.
limitations: Customer-reported.

rules.rationale: Very little RAM was available at scan time.
limitations: Android keeps RAM full by design; this is weak evidence on its own.

rules.rationale: A power source was detected but the battery was not charging during the scan.
limitations: Some computer USB ports supply too little power to charge; battery-protection features can pause charging.

rules.rationale: The phone was charging from the USB connection during the scan.
limitations: Charging at USB-computer currents does not prove fast charging works, nor that the port is free of intermittent faults.

rules.rationale: Charging that depends on the cable angle almost always means a worn or dirty port or a damaged cable.
limitations: Customer-reported.

rules.rationale: No charging response points to the cable, charger, port or charging circuit.
limitations: Customer-reported.

rules.rationale: Slow charging is often caused by a dirty port, a weak cable/charger, or a worn battery.
limitations: Customer-reported.

rules.rationale: Charging that stops partway can be a battery fault, overheating protection or a loose connection.
limitations: Battery-protection features (charge limit at 80-85%) cause the same behaviour on purpose.

rules.rationale: A different cable and charger work, so the original cable or charger is the likely culprit, not the phone.

notes.text: Your original cable or charger appears to be faulty. Replacing the accessory is much cheaper than a phone repair.

rules.rationale: The problem persists with a known-good cable and charger, which points to the phone.
Wireless charging works while cable charging does not, isolating the problem to the port side.
Neither wired nor wireless charging works, which points away from the port towards the battery or charging circuit.
Lint in the port is a very common cause of poor charging and is often fixed by careful cleaning.

notes.text: Try cleaning the port first (phone off, wooden or plastic toothpick, no liquids). Many 'broken' ports only need cleaning.

rules.rationale: Visibly bent or loose port parts mean the port needs repair.
limitations: Customer-reported.

rules.rationale: Residue in the port is a sign of liquid exposure and corrosion.
limitations: Customer-reported.

rules.rationale: The customer reports a charging problem.
limitations: Customer-reported symptom area only.

rules.rationale: The customer reports battery drain or unexpected shutdowns.
limitations: Customer-reported symptom area only.

rules.rationale: The OS has no touchscreen input device registered, which suggests the touch layer or its connector is not detected.
limitations: Output format of 'dumpsys input' varies; a parsing mismatch could produce a false result.

rules.rationale: Cracked glass, lines/ink spots, or a black screen on a phone that otherwise works indicate physical display damage.
limitations: Customer-reported; a cracked outer glass does not always mean the display panel is damaged.

rules.rationale: Flicker can come from a failing display or connector, and sometimes from software (adaptive brightness, refresh-rate bugs).
limitations: Customer-reported.

rules.rationale: Dead touch areas usually indicate a damaged touch layer.
limitations: Customer-reported; screen protectors and moisture can cause similar symptoms.

rules.rationale: Ghost touches are commonly caused by a damaged screen, a swelling battery pressing on it, or charger interference.
limitations: Customer-reported.

rules.rationale: Touch works normally.
Touch problems that a restart clears are more often software than hardware.
limitations: Early-stage hardware faults can also be intermittent.

rules.rationale: Touch problems that survive a restart are more likely hardware.
Impacts are the leading cause of display damage.
limitations: Many drops cause no damage.

rules.rationale: The customer reports a screen or touch problem.
limitations: Customer-reported symptom area only.

rules.rationale: The camera service reports no camera devices at all.
limitations: Could also be a camera service crash; restart and re-scan to confirm.

rules.rationale: A cracked lens, black preview, or a single failed lens points to a camera hardware fault.
limitations: Customer-reported.

rules.rationale: Persistent blur can be a damaged autofocus/stabilisation module, but is often a dirty lens or protector.
limitations: Clean the lens first.

rules.rationale: 'Camera failed' errors come from either the camera module or camera software.
limitations: Customer-reported.

rules.rationale: The camera works in another app, so the hardware is functioning and the default camera app is at fault.
The camera fails in every app, which points to the module or its connection.
The customer reports a camera problem.
limitations: Customer-reported symptom area only.

rules.rationale: A specific speaker, earpiece or microphone problem points to that component (or its grille being blocked).
limitations: Customer-reported; blocked grilles and Bluetooth routing cause similar symptoms.

rules.rationale: Audio problems limited to Bluetooth are a wireless connectivity issue, not a speaker fault.
limitations: The Bluetooth accessory itself may be at fault.

rules.rationale: Audio works through headphones, isolating the problem to the built-in speaker/earpiece.
No audio through any output suggests a software/audio-system problem rather than one speaker.
limitations: An audio codec hardware fault can also cause this.

rules.rationale: The customer reports an audio problem.
limitations: Customer-reported symptom area only.

rules.rationale: Airplane mode was on during the scan, which disables mobile radios by design.

notes.text: Airplane mode is switched ON. Turn it off and check whether the connectivity problem remains.

rules.rationale: The OS reports no SIM card, matching the customer's report.
limitations: The SIM may be unseated, damaged or deactivated rather than the phone's SIM reader.

notes.text: Re-seat the SIM card and, if possible, test another SIM before paying for a repair.

rules.rationale: The problem occurs everywhere while other phones work, pointing to this phone.
limitations: Customer-reported; account or carrier provisioning issues are also possible.

rules.rationale: Location-dependent problems usually reflect coverage or the network, not a phone fault.
The customer reports a connectivity problem.
limitations: Customer-reported symptom area only.

rules.rationale: Reported liquid exposure; speakers, microphones and charging ports are the parts most often affected.
limitations: Customer-reported; water-resistant phones often survive brief exposure.

rules.rationale: Recent exposure: damage may still be developing.

notes.text: Recent liquid exposure: power the phone off, do not charge it, and get it inspected. Charging a wet phone can cause short circuits.

rules.rationale: The customer reports no liquid exposure.
limitations: Exposure is sometimes unnoticed (humidity, rain in a pocket).

rules.rationale: Android's own storage benchmark measured slow writes (50 ms or more for a small write).
limitations: Single short benchmark; background activity can slow it. Not proof of a failing storage chip.

rules.rationale: The bootloader is unlocked or the system software is not the manufacturer's verified build.
limitations: Modified software is often stable; this only raises the chance of software-caused problems.

notes.text: This phone runs unlocked or modified system software. Some apps (e.g. banking) may refuse to run, official service centres may decline repairs, and resale value can be lower.

rules.rationale: During the colour test the customer saw lines, spots, dead pixels or patches.
limitations: Result judged by the customer during a guided test.

rules.rationale: The full-screen colour test showed no visible defects.
limitations: Result judged by the customer during a guided test.
Faint defects can be missed by eye.

rules.rationale: Some touchscreen squares did not register touches in the grid test.
limitations: Measured by the phone's browser while the customer dragged a finger; missed squares can also mean the finger skipped them.

rules.rationale: Every square of the touch grid registered a touch.
limitations: Does not test pressure, ghost touches over time or touch near the very edges.

rules.rationale: No sound was heard from the loudspeaker during the tone test.
limitations: Result judged by the customer during a guided test.
Check that the media volume is up and no Bluetooth device is connected.

rules.rationale: Test tones were quiet or distorted.
limitations: Result judged by the customer during a guided test.
A blocked grille causes the same; clean it gently first.

rules.rationale: Test tones were clear through the loudspeaker.
limitations: Result judged by the customer during a guided test.
Does not test the earpiece or microphone.

rules.rationale: The microphone level barely changed while the customer spoke.
limitations: Measured by the phone's browser; a phone case or finger over the microphone hole affects it.

rules.rationale: The microphone picked up the customer's voice at a normal level.
limitations: Only the microphone the browser selected was tested; phones have several.

rules.rationale: A camera did not start or stayed black in the camera test.
limitations: If other apps can use the camera, the browser permission may be the cause.

rules.rationale: The camera worked but the image was blurry, dark or stained.
limitations: Result judged by the customer during a guided test.
A dirty lens or lens cover causes the same; clean it first.

rules.rationale: The rear camera preview started (measured) and looked clear (customer judgement).
limitations: The browser uses one rear camera; other lenses are not tested.

rules.rationale: No vibration was felt during the vibration test.
limitations: Result judged by the customer during a guided test.

notes.text: The vibration motor did not respond in the test. Check that vibration is enabled in sound settings; if it is, a technician should inspect the motor.

rules.rationale: The motion sensors produced no changing readings.
limitations: The browser may block motion access.

notes.text: The motion sensors did not respond in the browser test. Auto-rotate and step counting may not work; a technician can confirm with the manufacturer's diagnostic app.

rules.rationale: At least one physical button did not respond.
limitations: Result judged by the customer during a guided test.

notes.text: A button did not respond. Remove the case (it can press or block buttons); if it persists, the button or its flex cable needs professional repair.

rules.rationale: The phone was connected to power for the whole test but never charged (battery below 80%).
limitations: Measured by the agent from the phone's own battery status. Some computer USB ports supply too little power; try a wall charger before paying for a repair.

rules.rationale: The power connection dropped while the plug was moved (measured by the agent), which is typical of a worn, loose or dirty charging port or a damaged cable.
limitations: Try another cable to rule out the cable itself.

rules.rationale: The connection stayed stable and the phone charged while the plug was moved.
limitations: Computer USB charging is slow; this does not test fast charging.

rules.rationale: The earpiece was silent or poor during a test call.
limitations: Result judged by the customer during a guided test.
Poor network coverage also degrades calls.

rules.rationale: A website did not load over mobile data.
limitations: Result judged by the customer during a guided test.
Data plans, APN settings and coverage can cause this.

rules.rationale: A website loaded over mobile data.
limitations: Result judged by the customer during a guided test.

rules.rationale: The bug report contains many app crashes or freezes.
limitations: Counts come from the logs still held by the phone; they show instability, not its root cause.

rules.rationale: The bug report records a system watchdog reset or kernel panic.
limitations: Counts come from the logs still held by the phone; they show instability, not its root cause.
Kernel panics can also come from hardware faults.

rules.rationale: Android repeatedly killed apps to free memory, which causes reloading and slowness.
limitations: Counts come from the logs still held by the phone; they show instability, not its root cause.
Some low-memory kills are normal on phones with little RAM.

rules.rationale: The bug report records a thermal shutdown.
limitations: Counts come from the logs still held by the phone; they show instability, not its root cause.
Heavy use in a hot place can cause this on a healthy phone.
